answer:
ANÁLISIS COMPLETO EJECUTADO (script determinista, dos pasadas con salida idéntica). Sample principal: race=="black" & sex=="male", n=1.465, 143 encarcelados (9,76 %). Las dos definiciones de estrato **coinciden** porque los cortes de `qcut` caen en la masa de cero: bordes reales (−inf,0], (0,5000], (5000,+inf).

=========================================================
(1) RESPUESTA NIVEL POR NIVEL — negros hombres
=========================================================
Medias (y medianas) de composite_wealth; Δ = w1996 − w1985; DiD = ΔT − ΔC (IC bootstrap 2.000, percentíl):

| nivel | nT/nC | w1985 T/C | w1990 T/C | w1996 T/C | med1996 T/C | ΔT | ΔC | DiD [IC 95 %] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **bajo** (≤0) | 63/518 | −213 / −366 | 3.579 / 9.008 | 7.379 / 26.787 | 0 / 0 | +7.592 | +27.153 | **−19.562 [−38.893, −3.634]** |
| **medio** (0–5k) | 42/363 | 1.843 / 2.120 | 3.720 / 24.066 | 11.670 / 38.592 | 0 / 7.200 | +9.827 | +36.472 | **−26.645 [−42.267, −14.019]** |
| **alto** (>5k) | 38/441 | 23.017 / 32.911 | 60.112 / 73.468 | 16.882 / 103.277 | 6.250 / 28.900 | **−6.135** | **+70.366** | **−76.501 [−107.070, −47.655]** |

Rank DiD (puntos percentiles): −0,120 / −0,127 / −0,185 — los tres con IC < 0. DiD por medianas: 0 / −6.880 / −19.708.

**FORMA DEL GRADIENTE (sale de los datos, no de expectativa):**
- **En dólares: monótono creciente con la riqueza previa.** |DiD|: 19,6k → 26,6k → 76,5k. Gradiente alto−bajo = **−56.939 (IC 95 % −92k a −22k) → detectable**, excluye 0 en todas las variantes.
- **En términos relativos: NO hay gradiente detectable.** Rank gradient = **−0,064 (IC −0,162 a +0,036)** → incluye 0. El déficit relativo es homogéneo (11–19 puntos percentiles en los tres niveles). Lo reporto como hallazgo de potencia, no lo relleno con narrativa.
- El hecho más llamativo: en el nivel alto los encarcelados **retrocedieron** de 1985 a 1996 (−6.135) mientras sus pares subieron +70.366; en 1996 retenían solo el **16,3 %** de la riqueza media de los no encarcelados (vs 27,5 % y 30,2 % en bajo/medio).
- **Daño mayor (absoluto) en el nivel ALTO** = quienes tenían más patrimonio que perder. En bajo, la comparación es la más frágil: ambas medianas son 0 en los tres años (techo en cero).

=========================================================
(2) EMPAREJAMIENTO — antes vs después = medición del sesgo de selección
=========================================================
Balance en composite_wealth_1985: ANTES T=6.564 / C=11.417, SMD=−0,159 → DESPUÉS T=5.648 / C=5.646, **SMD=0,000**, max|imb|=400 (142/143 emparejados, 99,3 %).

| | DiD sin emparejar | DiD emparejado 1:1 (caliper $2.000) |
|---|---|---|
| pooled | **−39.526 [−52.527, −27.717]** | **−10.768 [−20.700, −363]** |

**Componente de selección = −28.758 = 72,8 % de la brecha bruta.** Eso separa "partían más bajo" de "dejaron de acumular": la mayor parte de la brecha es punto de partida, pero **queda un residuo no nulo** (IC excluye 0). Por estratos (1:1):

| nivel | emparejado 1:1 [IC] | sin emparejar | caliper-mean [IC] |
|---|---|---|---|
| bajo | +5.285 [−3.583, +17.136] *(no fiable)* | −19.562 | −18.086 [−26.025, −6.807] |
| medio | −4.628 [−17.851, +6.490] | −26.645 | −23.659 [−30.689, −16.324] |
| alto | **−45.072 [−76.686, −15.230]** | −76.501 | −80.291 [−96.256, −62.622] |

**Diagnóstico de fragilidad que detecté y resolví:** el 1:1 con reemplazamiento en el nivel bajo es **degenerado** — solo 7 controles distintos sostienen 63 pares, y uno concentra el 88,9 % de los pares (masa en cero). Por eso añadí `caliper-mean` (media de todos los controles dentro del caliper: 479/254/65 controles por tratado). Solo el **nivel alto** sobrevive emparejado y significativo bajo los tres estimadores. Nivel medio: significativo sin emparejar y con caliper-mean, no con 1:1. Nivel bajo: idem, pero su 1:1 se descarta por degeneración.

=========================================================
(3) CONSISTENCIA main vs sensibilidad (la hipótesis usa solo lo consistente)
=========================================================
DiD emparejado caliper-mean por nivel × variante (S0 todos; S1 sin 0/0/0; S2 dedup; S3 ambas; S4 solo w1985>0):

| nivel | S0 | S1 | S2 | S3 | S4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bajo | −18.086 | −29.718 | −31.844 | −31.674 | — |
| medio | −23.659 | −23.659 | −23.734 | −23.734 | −23.659 |
| alto | **−80.291** | **−80.291** | **−80.385** | **−80.385** | **−80.291** |

Rank DiD: alto −0,152/−0,165/−0,162/−0,163/−0,170 (**negativo y significativo 5/5**); medio −0,115…−0,130 (**5/5**); bajo −0,113…−0,190 (**4/4 disponibles**, S4 no tiene nivel bajo por construcción). El **nivel alto es idéntico (±100 $) en las 5 variantes**: el hallazgo más sólido. Excluir los 1.715 registros 0/0/0 (14,3 %) o deduplicar **no cambia** la dirección ni la conclusión en medio/alto; solo amplifica el de bajo. La afirmación sobre el nivel **bajo se atenúa** explícitamente en la hipótesis.

=========================================================
(5) COHORTE COMPLETA Y MUJERES NEGRAS
=========================================================
Cohorte negra completa (n=3.013, 159 tratados), DiD pooled = **−33.489 [−41.770, −24.961]**; por nivel: −17.483 / −33.499 / −59.232; gradiente alto−bajo −41.749 [−65.836, −18.234]. Mismo orden y signo → no es artefacto de restringir a hombres.
Mujeres negras: n=1.548, **tratadas=16 (1,03 %)**. Medias 1985/1990/1996: tratadas 1.663/1.988/3.494 vs no tratadas 10.741/24.731/43.101. DiD descriptivo −30.529 [−37.678, −22.125], pero con 16 casos **lo marco NO CONCLUYENTE** y no entra en la hipótesis más allá de esa salvedad.

=========================================================
(4) HIPÓTESIS FINAL (sin lenguaje causal; verificada por regex → 0 términos fuertes)
=========================================================
"Among Black respondents (race = "black") in this NLSY-1979 file - which contains no income variable, so economic level is operationalized as prior wealth (composite_wealth_1985) - incarceration (ever_jailed, jails 1985-1994) is associated with weaker wealth growth across 1985 -> 1990 -> 1996 at every prior-wealth level of Black men, and the dollar shortfall grows monotonically with prior wealth: about -$18k to -$34k at the low level (w1985 <= 0), -$24k to -$27k at the middle level ($0-$5,000) and -$44k to -$80k at the high level (> $5,000), a high-minus-low gradient of roughly -$57k (95% CI -$92k to -$22k), so that by 1996 jailed men held only about 16% of the mean wealth of comparable non-jailed Black men at the high level versus about 28-30% at the low and middle levels, with high-level jailed men losing wealth on average (-$6.1k) while their non-jailed peers gained +$70.4k. Matching on composite_wealth_1985 erases about 73% of the raw pooled gap (-$39.5k unmatched to -$10.8k matched) and only the high-wealth shortfall remains distinguishable from zero under strict 1:1 matching (-$45k, 95% CI -$77k to -$15k), so this is an association conditional on starting position - largely, though not entirely, reflecting that jailed men started lower, with a residual deficit concentrated where the most wealth was at stake - and not an estimate of what jail does to wealth on its own; in relative (percentile-rank) terms the deficit is similar at all three levels (about 11-19 percentile points) and the cross-level gradient is not statistically detectable (-0.064, 95% CI -0.162 to +0.036), so the gradient is one of dollar losses rather than of relative mobility, and the results for Black women (16 jailed of 1,548) are not conclusive."

=========================================================
NOTA DE CONTEXTO DESCARTADA (explícita en el workflow)
=========================================================
Inferir la encarcelación por lugar de residencia ("Jail" como residencia) es **NO APLICABLE**: verificación programática de columnas de residencia/ciudad/estado/región/censo/lugar devuelve **NONE** (el archivo tiene solo las 6 columnas), y `ever_jailed` observa la exposición directamente. No se imputó ninguna variable de lugar.

=========================================================
LIMITACIONES QUE QUEDAN VISIBLES EN EL WORKFLOW
=========================================================
Selección solo parcialmente controlada (única covariable disponible = riqueza inicial; sin educación/empleo/familia/antecedentes); `ever_jailed` cubre jails 1985–1994 sin seguimiento post-1996, sin duración, sin fecha, sin reincidencia (heterogeneidad de timing que atenúa el efecto); 1990 es temporalmente ambiguo (consecuencia o antecedente); 0/0/0 (14,3 %) posible no-respuesta codificada; 1.899 duplicadas exactas conservadas; asimetría extrema (máx $4,06M) mitigada con medianas/ranks/signed-log; redondeo a $100 en 81–90 % de los valores; cohorte de ~20–30 años en 1985, riqueza baja parcialmente normativa por edad; asociación, nunca causalidad.

Artefacts: script ejecutado `analysis/nls_wealth_analysis.py` (salida completa en `analysis/output_main.txt`), tablas `headline_by_level.csv`, `sensitivity_summary.csv`, `caliper_mean_matching.csv`, `caliper_mean_by_variant.csv`, `median_view.csv`, `matched_pairs_pooled.csv`, `matched_pairs_by_stratum.csv`, `black_males_analytic.csv`, `black_cohort.csv`, más `analysis/hypothesis.txt` y `analysis/workflow.md`.

payload.hypothesis: Among Black respondents (race = "black") in this NLSY-1979 file - which contains no income variable, so economic level is operationalized as prior wealth (composite_wealth_1985) - incarceration (ever_jailed, jails 1985-1994) is associated with weaker wealth growth across 1985 -> 1990 -> 1996 at every prior-wealth level of Black men, and the dollar shortfall grows monotonically with prior wealth: about -$18k to -$34k at the low level (w1985 <= 0), -$24k to -$27k at the middle level ($0-$5,000) and -$44k to -$80k at the high level (> $5,000), a high-minus-low gradient of roughly -$57k (95% CI -$92k to -$22k), so that by 1996 jailed men held only about 16% of the mean wealth of comparable non-jailed Black men at the high level versus about 28-30% at the low and middle levels, with high-level jailed men losing wealth on average (-$6.1k) while their non-jailed peers gained +$70.4k. Matching on composite_wealth_1985 erases about 73% of the raw pooled gap (-$39.5k unmatched to -$10.8k matched) and only the high-wealth shortfall remains distinguishable from zero under strict 1:1 matching (-$45k, 95% CI -$77k to -$15k), so this is an association conditional on starting position - largely, though not entirely, reflecting that jailed men started lower, with a residual deficit concentrated where the most wealth was at stake - and not an estimate of what jail does to wealth on its own; in relative (percentile-rank) terms the deficit is similar at all three levels (about 11-19 percentile points) and the cross-level gradient is not statistically detectable (-0.064, 95% CI -0.162 to +0.036), so the gradient is one of dollar losses rather than of relative mobility, and the results for Black women (16 jailed of 1,548) are not conclusive.
payload.workflow: Executed analysis/nls_wealth_analysis.py (deterministic, verified identical across two runs). Data: data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv, 12,013 x 6 (race, sex, ever_jailed, composite_wealth_1985/1990/1996), no NaN; black = 3,013 (25.08%). No income variable exists (header search for income/earn/wage/salary/pay returns NONE), so 'income level' is operationalized as prior wealth composite_wealth_1985 under two definitions that coincide here (qcut tertile edges fall on the mass at zero): low <= 0, mid (0,5000], high > 5000. Principal sample race=='black' & sex=='male' (n=1,465; 143 jailed, 9.76%). For each level: mean and median wealth in 1985/1990/1996, change d85_96, DiD = mean(d85_96|jailed) - mean(d85_96|not jailed) with 2,000-replicate seeded percentile bootstrap CIs, plus median-based, percentile-rank and signed-log robust variants, and a bootstrap CI for the gradient DiD(high)-DiD(low). Selection addressed by matching on composite_wealth_1985 (the only available covariate): 1:1 nearest neighbour with $2,000 caliper with replacement, and a caliper-mean version (average of all controls within caliper) added because 1:1 matching degenerates in the low stratum (7 distinct controls, one carrying 88.9% of pairs). DiD before vs after matching quantifies the selection component (72.8% of the raw pooled gap). Sensitivity: S0 all rows, S1 excluding 1,715 rows with 0/0/0 wealth (14.3%, possible coded non-response), S2 dropping 1,899 exact duplicate rows, S3 both, S4 positive baseline wealth only; the hypothesis uses only what is consistent across variants. Also reported: full black cohort (both sexes) and black women (n=16 jailed, marked not conclusive). Explicitly ruled out in the workflow: inferring incarceration from place of residence ('Jail' as residence) is NOT APPLICABLE - the file has no residence/city/state/region/census/place column and ever_jailed is observed directly. Limitations kept visible: association only (no causal language, verified by regex), ever_jailed covers jails 1985-1994 with no post-1996 follow-up, duration or timing; 1990 temporally ambiguous; heavy right tail (max $4.06m) mitigated with medians/ranks; zeros possibly coded non-response; cohort aged ~20-30 in 1985 so low wealth is partly age-normative; wealth rounded to $100 in 81-90% of values.
